root_motivation: Three rustbuild PRDs (rustbuild-hermetic-scope, autobuilder-rollback-tag-aware, rollback-redeploy-tag-onboard) have finished code, green AC tests, and clean clippy, but the shared gate has reported the identical 6-of-25 block set for over 20 hours and ~15 concurrent ticks, always dismissed as "pre-existing, out of scope." This PRD is the first to actually run each blocking receipt fresh and read its real cause instead of re-citing the prior tick's prose — three of the six turn out to be concretely fixable in-repo, not host-wide mysteries: a `cargo-deny` bans/advisories failure, a self-hosted test that can never pass on a fresh checkout, and an empty risk-gate receipt. A fourth (CI) is real but is a human GitHub-account check, not a code fix. Pay this once so the rustbuild trio (and whatever lands next) can actually reach `built`.
user_persona: The autobuilder skill orchestrator (a Claude session) and the human invoking `/autobuilder` from their own project. Both shell out to this binary for the receipt + gate steps that must not live in bash.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given the 4 wildcard path dependencies now carry explicit `version =`, When `cargo deny check bans` runs, Then it no longer reports the wildcard-dependency error for any of them.
Given the anyhow lockfile bump, When `cargo deny check advisories` runs, Then the RUSTSEC advisory against `anyhow` is resolved and `cargo test --workspace` stays fully green apart from item 3 below.

Given the AC-X1 fix, When `cargo test --workspace` runs on a fresh checkout with no pre-existing `target/release` binaries, Then `acceptance_ac_x1_helps` passes without requiring an out-of-band `cargo build --release` first.

Given items 1-3 landed, When `scripts/run-metrics.sh` runs standalone, Then AC6 passes and `ac_passing_count == ac_total_count` (7/7), so `autobuilder loop --iteration 0 --trace` reports `verdict != crash`.
Given the risk-gate emission fix, When a normal loop iteration runs, Then `target/autobuilder/receipts/risk-gate.json` is non-empty and parses as valid `autobuilder.bad_rust_audit.v1`.

Given all of the above, When `extend-gate.sh /home/jsy/wintermute/rustbuild --head <landed sha>` runs, Then the blocking set no longer contains `proof-receipt`, `risk-gate`, or the bans/advisories portion of `reviewer-agent`'s `block_reasons` (`intake`, `ci-checks`, and `secrets-scan` may still block per the Problem section's documented structural/human-decision/by-design causes).

Given the finished diff, When version and tests are checked, Then `Cargo.toml` is bumped patch, `cargo test --workspace` is fully green, and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean on the diff.

scope: Stage 4 risk gate (7 receipts + release receipt)
non_goals: Spawning Claude subagents from the binary itself (that is the orchestrator's job)
Web-service, WASM, or embedded scaffolding (v1 supports cli + lib only)
Auto-applying self-evolution proposals (always gated for user review)
Re-running the underlying audit/test commands inside `gate` (gate only attests; producers own the work)

five_whys_trace.q: Why a Rust companion binary instead of a pure-skill scaffold?
five_whys_trace.a: Shell is too easy to subvert (set -e off, grep eaten, jq missing). The load-bearing parts — metric extraction, digest binding, schema validation — need a typed implementation under tests.

five_whys_trace.q: Why a 7-receipt gate instead of `cargo test && cargo clippy`?
five_whys_trace.a: Each receipt covers a class of failure that the others miss: clippy doesn't see CI status, tests don't see proof-lane routing, and none of them produce an independent-review record. The gate is what makes 'ready' falsifiable.

five_whys_trace.q: Why bootstrap autobuilder against itself before running it on other projects?
five_whys_trace.a: If the gate model can't certify the binary that produces gate receipts, it can't be trusted on any other project. The meta-bootstrap is the cheapest adversarial test of the whole pipeline.

five_whys_trace.q: Why deny unwrap/expect everywhere in src/ when most of this is glue code?
five_whys_trace.a: Glue code that panics on a missing receipt or malformed JSON destroys the audit trail at exactly the moments the gate matters most. Erroring back to the caller keeps the diagnostic surface alive.

five_whys_trace.q: Why digest-bind every receipt instead of trusting file timestamps?
five_whys_trace.a: Timestamps lie under git checkout. A self-binding sha256 lets the gate detect tampering and lets reviewers re-verify by recomputing on the receipt's own contents.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Where does the autobuilder repo's 'project' live for the gate — repo root or autobuilder/ workspace?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Repo root. agent/, scripts/, target/autobuilder/ all sit at /home/jsy/projects/autobuilder/. Proof-lanes globs use autobuilder/src/** prefix to match `git diff` output.
